focus_area: AiJobCriteria model + Job criteria methods + the entire zero-criteria guard chain end-to-end (model constant -> writer sites -> predicate -> validators -> bulk queue -> scoring funnel -> completion broadcast)

findings.title: latest_ai_job_criteria / latest_succeeded_ai_job_criteria order by created_at with no id tiebreak (non-deterministic on exact ties)
findings.description: latest_ai_job_criteria (job.rb:688 `ai_job_criteria.order(created_at: :desc).first`) and latest_succeeded_ai_job_criteria (job.rb:692-693) sort only by created_at. When two rows share an identical created_at timestamp, Postgres row order among the tied rows is undefined, so the 'latest' row is not deterministic. The one realistic tie is the documented double-POST case (SPEC 4.1: extract_job_criteria_immediately does NOT guard pending, so two rapid POSTs can create two pending rows in the same instant) — but both tied rows are `pending`, so zero_criteria_extraction_failure? returns false either way and no behavior changes. This is NOT actionable: it exactly matches the established codebase/analog pattern (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb:18,60 and textract_result.rb:81 all use `.order(created_at: :desc).first` with no id tiebreak; job.rb:808-810 most_recent_what_jobs_listing too). Recorded only as an observation.
findings.recommendation: No action required — matches the analog and has no reachable wrong-result path. If ever hardened, add a secondary `.order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc)` uniformly across the latest-row helpers, but only alongside the analog.

findings.title: extract_job_criteria_immediately issues two identical latest_ai_job_criteria queries
findings.description: extract_job_criteria_immediately calls latest_ai_job_criteria twice (job.rb:732 `latest_ai_job_criteria&.status_in_progress?` and job.rb:733 `latest_ai_job_criteria&.status_retrying?`), firing two identical SELECTs, whereas the sibling methods auto_extract_job_criteria (job.rb:703) and extract_job_criteria (job.rb:720) cache the row once into existing_ai_job_criteria and reuse it. Pure micro-inefficiency on a single-record code path; no correctness impact. Also note this is verbatim the SPEC 4.1 code block, so it matches the approved spec exactly.
findings.recommendation: No action required (spec-verbatim). If touched later, memoize into a local like the sibling methods for consistency.
